queries.query: LLM "network configuration" generation OR "network config" "large language model"
queries.rationale: Direct literature on using LLMs to generate network configurations or translate intent-to-configuration (core phenomenon).
Empirical and analytic work describing hallucination or incorrect factual outputs by LLMs in NetOps contexts (failure phenomenon).

queries.query: intent-based networking verification "intent to configuration" "verification" Batfish
queries.rationale: Work on intent-based networking and verification tools that could serve as validators or baselines (neighbouring and mitigation mechanisms).
Papers and systems that use a generate-validate-repair loop with LLMs—key architectural mitigation pattern for NetOps correctness.

queries.query: formal verification network configurations SMT SAT "network verification"
queries.rationale: Formal/deterministic verification methods (SMT, SAT, model checking) for network configs to compare or integrate with LLM outputs.

queries.query: constrained decoding "LLM" "constrained generation" syntactic constraints network config
queries.rationale: Generation-time mitigation strategies (constrained decoding, grammar-constrained generation) applicable to config synthesis.

queries.query: tool-augmented LLMs chain-of-thought tool use "retrieval-augmented generation" "tool use"
queries.rationale: Mechanisms where LLMs call tools or retrieve state (e.g., network state) — affects correctness and reproducibility in NetOps workflows.
Work on bounded iterative correction/self-refinement of LLM outputs relevant for repair of configurations or plans.
Survey and critique of existing AIOps/NetOps benchmarks that might be reused or whose validity must be questioned.

queries.query: limitations benchmarks "LLM" "networking" synthetic vs real data external validity
queries.rationale: Methodological analyses of benchmark validity, synthetic-data pitfalls, and external validity—critical when designing NetOps evaluations.
Operationally meaningful metrics for correctness (reachability, isolation, ACL compliance, performance regressions) to evaluate LLM outputs.

queries.query: network emulation Mininet container-based emulation "testbed" evaluation "NetOps"
queries.rationale: Execution and evaluation environments (Mininet, ns-3, emulation/testbed setups) for validating LLM-generated configs safely.
Work on human oversight, alerting, and trust calibration for operator workflows when integrating LLMs into NetOps.
source_preferences: HCI conferences (CHI) for human oversight studies

queries.rationale: General research on safety and risk of agentic systems operating on critical infrastructure—contextualises autonomous NetOps risks.
Specific tool-focused search (Batfish and similar) for concrete verification capabilities and prior comparative evaluations.
Broader literature on intent-based networking and intent translation pipelines, as an adjacent domain with established formalization efforts.
source_preferences: industry whitepapers (Cisco, Juniper) if cited with evidence

inclusion_criteria: Primary research papers (peer-reviewed or preprints) that present empirical results, methods, or systems relevant to LLMs/NetOps.
Tool, dataset, or benchmark descriptions with public artifacts (code, data, reproducible evaluation).
Formal methods and verification literature applicable to network configuration correctness.
Surveys, systematic reviews, and rigorous position papers that contextualize NetOps+LLM risks or methods.
RFCs, standards, and authoritative operational documents when used to define operational correctness criteria.
exclusion_criteria: Unsubstantiated blog posts, opinion pieces, or vendor marketing without verifiable empirical evidence or public artifacts.
Proprietary internal reports unavailable to public scrutiny.
Papers unrelated to networks or operations (purely NLP tasks without NetOps application).
Works that only benchmark general LLM knowledge (e.g., trivia) without operational validation or NetOps relevance.
date_rationale: Collect foundational work (formal verification, intent-based networking) across the last 10–15 years while prioritizing the rapid-progress LLM and AIOps literature from ~2020–2026 to capture recent mechanisms (tooling, RAG, agentic systems) and the latest benchmarks and mitigation strategies.
